Group-level whole-brain fMRI contrasts from a task about learning others' preferences vs self meet the global criteria and directly measure social processing (self–other preference learning, mentalising).
The Different>Similar contrast compares agents who differ vs match participant preferences, directly indexing social comparison related to liking/trust (affiliation); global criteria satisfied.
Contrast does not target social communication (facial/affective communication or production/reception of communicative signals). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The contrast reflects agent choices in relation to participant choices (self–other comparison); meets global criteria and assays self-related processing in a social comparison context.
Contrast measures observers' processing of others' choices (ASim vs ADiff), satisfying global criteria and targeting perception/understanding of others.
Negative PE_Sim conjunction is a whole-brain group fMRI result indexing unexpected dissimilarity of agents relative to the participant—this is social processing of self–other preference information.
The effect is localized to visual/attention areas tracking unexpected dissimilarity and does not directly measure affiliation/attachment. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This analysis does not assess social communication (facial/affective reception or production). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
PE_Sim is computed relative to the participant's choices (self reference); the conjunction identifies areas responsive to unexpected dissimilarity and meets the perception-self criteria.
This conjunction tracks responses to others' choices (unexpected dissimilar choices by agents) and therefore meets perception-of-others criteria.
Positive AC conjunction (dmPFC) is a whole-brain group result indexing accumulated consistency of agents relative to self—this is social processing (impression formation/learning).

AC (accumulated consistency) relates to impression formation and affiliation (study links similarity to liking/trust); the conjunction in dmPFC indexes person-specific similarity relevant to affiliation.
AC tracking in dmPFC reflects impression/consistency learning rather than communicative exchange; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
AC explicitly models how each agent's choices align with the participant over time (self-referential evidence); meets perception-self criteria.
AC tracks properties of other agents (their consistency) across trials; this satisfies perception-of-others inclusion criteria.
Positive PE_Con conjunction (caudate) is a whole-brain group-level effect indexing prediction errors about others' choice consistency relative to the participant—this is social processing.
PE_Con in the caudate indexes value/update signals for consistency but does not directly measure affiliation/attachment (no explicit affiliation contrast). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This analysis indexes prediction errors for social learning rather than communicative processes; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
PE_Con is computed as the difference between an agent's choice and the participant-based expectation (self-referenced model); meets perception-self criteria.
PE_Con reflects updates about other agents' behavior; this directly addresses perception/understanding of others.
Negative PE_Con conjunction (mentalising regions) indexes unexpected inconsistency of agents' choices relative to participant expectations—a social processing signal meeting global criteria.
Negative PE_Con highlights mentalising responses to inconsistency but does not directly operationalize affiliation/attachment. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This contrast indexes prediction-error responses in social-cognition regions, not communicative reception/production. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
PE_Con is defined relative to participant-based expectations about agents (self-referenced), and these regions respond to unexpected deviations—meets perception-self criteria.
Negative PE_Con activates regions involved in reasoning about others' behaviour (mentalising network), satisfying perception-of-others criteria.

Contrast examines perception of vocal emotional signals (joy vs tickle) — receptive non-facial social communication; group-level whole-brain task contrast in healthy adults.
Task does not index self-related processing or self-awareness judgments; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 not satisfied.
Contrast probes perception/understanding of others' emotional vocalizations (joy vs tickle), requiring inference about sender's emotional state; meets group whole-brain criteria.
Healthy adult, group-level whole-brain contrast comparing taunt vs tickle; probes social-emotional processing of laughter types.
Does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs (no kinship, close-relationship, cooperation/competition stimuli); AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 not satisfied.
Taunt vs tickle contrasts receptive vocal emotional signals (non-facial social communication) in healthy adults at group-level.
No self-related judgments or self-awareness measures; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 not satisfied.
Contrast assesses understanding of others' emotional vocalizations (taunt vs tickle), involving inference about sender state; meets global criteria.
Conjunction of JOY>TIC and TAU>TIC isolates emotional (socially salient) laughter vs tickle — directly probes social processing of laughter types in healthy adults at group level.
Does not index affiliation/attachment constructs (no measures of bonding/kinship/cooperation); AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 not satisfied.
Conjunction contrast targets perception of socially communicative emotional laughter (receptive vocal communication) — fits social communication construct; group-level whole-brain map.
No self-related processing evaluated in this contrast; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 not satisfied.
Conjunction isolates regions sensitive to emotional (socially salient) laughter independent of valence — reflects understanding/perception of others' emotional states; global criteria satisfied.
Tickle>Joy contrast is a group-level whole-brain comparison of laughter types probing social/acoustic aspects of laughter perception in healthy adults.
Not a measure of affiliation/attachment (no bonding/kinship/cooperation manipulations); AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 not satisfied.

Tickle>Taunt is a group-level whole-brain contrast comparing laughter types that probes social and acoustic processing of vocalizations in healthy adults.
No affiliation/attachment constructs are measured; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 not satisfied.
Contrast concerns perception of vocal emotional signals (tickle vs taunt) — receptive non-facial social communication at group-level.
No self-related measures in this contrast; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 not satisfied.
Differentiates perception/understanding of others' vocal emotional states (tickle vs taunt); meets global whole-brain healthy adult criteria.

Not measuring affiliation/attachment constructs; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 not satisfied.
